hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated manganate(VII) does to a C=C bond, it completely cleaves it rather than just adding OH groups.
Draw out 2-methylbut-2-ene as $\text{CH}_3\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CHCH}_3$ and notice the left C has two alkyl groups while the right C has one H.
Remember that under hot, vigorous conditions any aldehyde fragment formed is oxidised straight on to a carboxylic acid, while a ketone fragment stops.
walkthrough:
**Draw the alkene structure**

Think of the double bond as the breaking point. Let us write the structure clearly.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$$
This is 2-methylbut-2-ene. C-2 has two $\text{CH}_3$ groups, C-3 has one $\text{CH}_3$ and one H.

**Cleave the double bond**

Hot, concentrated $\text{MnO}_4^-$ / $\text{H}^+$ breaks the C=C completely. Each C of the double bond becomes a C=O.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$>\text{C}=\text{C}< \; \xrightarrow{hot, conc. \text{MnO}_4^-} \; >\text{C}=\text{O} + \text{O}=\text{C}<$$

**Identify the two carbonyl fragments**

The $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ end with no H must become a ketone. The $\text{CHCH}_3$ end with one H first becomes an aldehyde.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{C}= \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 \text{ (propanone)}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}= \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \text{ (ethanal, initially)}$$

**Apply further oxidation under vigorous conditions**

This is the key exam point. Aldehydes are easily oxidised further by hot oxidiser, ketones are not.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
So final products are propanone, which stops, plus ethanoic acid, from further oxidation of ethanal.

options.A: This stops one step too early. Ethanal is indeed the first fragment from the right-hand side, but with hot, concentrated manganate(VII) it does not survive and is oxidised on to ethanoic acid.
options.B: Correct and complete. Cleavage gives $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O}$ which is propanone, and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=O}$ which is ethanal. Under hot, vigorous oxidation the ethanal is further oxidised to $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, ethanoic acid.
options.C: Ethanoic acid is right, but propan-2-ol is wrong. Oxidative cleavage of alkenes gives carbonyl compounds (C=O), never alcohols (C-OH). The left-hand $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=$ fragment must give the ketone propanone.
options.D: Both alcohols are wrong. This confuses vigorous cleavage with mild hydroxylation. Hot, concentrated $\text{MnO}_4^-$ breaks the C=C to give C=O compounds, and any aldehyde is then oxidised to an acid, so no ethanol or propan-2-ol forms.
